decisions.summary: Work order: survey (T01), call-count watch (US5), cheap wins/single-site (US2), wells (US3), pairwise outside the lanes, lane web and law last after feature 417.
decisions.why: Matches request.md 5's approved order clause for clause.

decisions.summary: The plan holds T01 only; each later task is filed with its own section after the survey has run.
decisions.why: FR-002 requires engine tasks to be scoped against the survey's output on the then-current engine; deferring them is that requirement, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: perf-fanout is a by-hand diagnostic, never a gate; report committed under dev/perf-log, .prof files in gitignored dev/perf-raw; stdlib cProfile/pstats.
decisions.why: Consistent with request.md 4: gating is the call-count flag (US5/FR-006), not the survey; storage and libraries narrow nothing asked.

decisions.summary: The 427-start bookend is taken before the first engine task (T02), not before T01.
decisions.why: T01 changes no stage, so the bookend measures the same engine either way; FR-005 is still met.

decisions.summary: make perf-fanout with SEED/HOUSEHOLDS/STAGES/HOT/JOBS/LABEL, per-stage totals and growth exponent, multiplier chains by the reference walk kept as written, fastest growers, report to dev/perf-log.
decisions.why: FR-001 and SC-001: built as tooling-perf-fanout.md designs it; it lists every 50k+ chain with its anchor.

decisions.summary: JOBS defaults to 3 instead of the design note's 5, citing the shared 10 GB memory cap read at 9.1-9.3 GB.
decisions.why: Changes only the default parallelism: output identical, overridable on the command line, and the GM's words say nothing about job count. A departure from tooling-perf-fanout.md's default that narrows no reach.

decisions.summary: Lands through make land rather than the design note's make land-tooling, because a module under l7r/ is engine by ci/delta.is_engine.
decisions.why: FR-001's 'on its own' is kept and the route taken is the stricter one, so the deliverable is not narrowed. Rests on a premise about ci/delta.is_engine not verifiable from the bundle; placing the module outside l7r/ to honor 'as tooling' literally is a design choice, not a fidelity finding.

decisions.summary: Exits: 'FR-008 green: landed with its fresh rate. Red: the failing seeds recorded and the task set down, a claim that it cannot be placed correctly ruled through make arbiter-ask (D11, D35).'
decisions.why: Template text from another feature: FR-008 is 'the engine stays in Python', not a landing condition; D11 and D35 exist nowhere in this plan or spec-cited.md; 'placed correctly' and 'fresh rate' are placement/seed-pass language for a tool that changes no stage. As written, the red exit sets T01 down on 'failing seeds'. T01 cannot make a seed regress (FR-007), so the only failing seeds at its landing are ones already failing on HEAD, and request.md 4 ('should not require all seeds to pass if seeds were previously failing') and 5 ('not have a requirement to have all of our seeds pass') exclude exactly that as a reason. It abandons the requested survey on a condition the GM ruled out: not physically necessary, not implied by the GM's words (they say the opposite), not serving the purpose. Fix: green = tests red without D1 and make perf-fanout on the current engine compared with research/fanout-2026-10-26.txt (FR-001, SC-001); red = only a seed passing on HEAD that fails after (FR-007); strike FR-008, D11, D35, 'placed correctly', 'fresh rate'.
